questions.stem: The VIJAYANAGARA empire was founded in 1336 CE by:

options.option_text: HARIHARA I and BUKKA RAYA I (Sangama dynasty) — founded under the guidance of sage VIDYARANYA of Sringeri

questions.explanation: VIJAYANAGARA EMPIRE (1336-1646 CE) — south Indian kingdom on the TUNGABHADRA river; capital HAMPI (modern Karnataka). FOUNDED by brothers HARIHARA I and BUKKA RAYA I (also called Hakka and Bukka), originally treasury officials of KAKATIYAS of Warangal; captured by DELHI SULTANATE (Muhammad bin Tughluq), converted to Islam, sent south to govern; re-converted back to Hinduism under sage VIDYARANYA of Sringeri Math; raised the banner of Hindu resurgence against Islamic expansion. ORIGINAL NAME of the city: VIJAYANAGARA (‘City of Victory’); also called ‘Bidarahalli’ ‘Virupakshapura’. Four DYNASTIES ruled successively: (1) SANGAMA (1336-1485) — founders; included Harihara, Bukka, Deva Raya I & II. (2) SALUVA (1485-1505) — founded by Saluva Narasimha. (3) TULUVA (1491-1570) — KRISHNADEVARAYA (1509-1529) the GREATEST; golden age. (4) ARAVIDU (1542-1646) — last dynasty after Battle of Talikota. Empire became the southernmost HINDU bastion against Bahmani/Deccan Sultanates; lasted 310 years. Foreign travellers: NICOLO DE CONTI (Italian, Deva Raya II's court), ABDUR RAZZAQ (Persian, Deva Raya II's court), DOMINGO PAES (Portuguese, Krishnadevaraya's), FERNAO NUNIZ (Portuguese, Achyutadevaraya's) — all left detailed accounts.

questions.stem: The GREATEST ruler of the Vijayanagara empire, who presided over its golden age (1509-1529), was:

options.option_text: KRISHNADEVARAYA (Tuluva dynasty) — poet-king, author of ‘Amuktamalyada’ (Telugu); patron of the ASHTADIGGAJAS

questions.explanation: KRISHNADEVARAYA (1509-1529) — son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka; the MOST CELEBRATED Vijayanagara ruler; empire reached its ZENITH politically, militarily, culturally, commercially. MILITARY: (1) Defeated GAJAPATIS of Odisha (Prataparudra Deva) and took Udayagiri, Kondavidu; (2) crushed ADIL SHAH of Bijapur at battle of Raichur (1520) — pivotal Deccan victory; (3) extended empire from Krishna-Godavari in north to Cape Comorin in south, west to Konkan, east to Bay of Bengal. LITERATURE & LEARNING: (1) himself a scholar — patronised TELUGU, KANNADA, TAMIL, SANSKRIT. (2) His AMUKTAMALYADA (Telugu) a manual of kingship — ‘a king should always be mindful of his subjects’ welfare’; also Sanskrit JAMBAVATI KALYANAM. (3) Court had ASHTADIGGAJAS (‘eight elephants of literature’) — ALLASANI PEDDANA (‘Andhra Kavita Pitamaha’, author of Manucharitra), NANDI THIMMANA, MADAYYAGARI MALLANA, DHURJATI, AYYALARAJU RAMABHADRUDU, PINGALI SURANA, RAMARAJABHUSHANA, TENALI RAMAKRISHNA (the wit). (4) Patronised HARIHARA KANAKADASA, VYASARAYA (Madhva saint-composer). ARCHITECTURE: built HAZARA RAMA temple, VITTHALA (with Stone Chariot), KRISHNA temple (to house Krishna idol brought from Udayagiri), upgraded VIRUPAKSHA; built suburb NAGALAPURAM (after queen Nagala Devi). DIPLOMACY: cordial relations with PORTUGUESE (Albuquerque); exchanged embassies. TRADE: Goa/ Bhatkal / Mangalore ports bustling.

questions.stem: The battle of TALIKOTA (1565) that led to the DOWNFALL of Vijayanagara was fought between:

options.option_text: Vijayanagara and the Bahmani Sultanate (still undivided)
VIJAYANAGARA (under RAMA RAYA, regent of Sadashiva Raya) vs a CONFEDERACY of four Deccan Sultanates: BIJAPUR (Adil Shahi) + AHMADNAGAR (Nizam Shahi) + GOLCONDA (Qutb Shahi) + BIDAR (Barid Shahi)

questions.explanation: BATTLE OF TALIKOTA / RAKKASA-TANGADI (23 January 1565) — fought on the banks of KRISHNA river at a place variously called TALIKOTA, RAKKASI-TANGADI, or BANNIHATTI (near Bijapur). KEY DETAILS: (1) VIJAYANAGARA was then ruled by SADASHIVA RAYA (nominal), with RAMA RAYA the de facto regent — an aggressive statesman who had earlier played Deccan Sultans off against each other. (2) Alarmed by his dominance, FOUR DECCAN SULTANATES formed a CONFEDERACY — BIJAPUR (Ali Adil Shah I), AHMADNAGAR (Hussain Nizam Shah I), GOLCONDA (Ibrahim Qutb Shah), BIDAR (Ali Barid Shah). (Berar’s Imad Shahi had been absorbed earlier.) Cemented via marriages. (3) VIJAYANAGARA army (c. 1.4 lakh) initially had the upper hand; but TWO Muslim COMMANDERS in Rama Raya's army (Gilani brothers) DEFECTED mid-battle, tipping the tide. (4) RAMA RAYA was captured and BEHEADED on the spot by Hussain Nizam Shah. (5) Defeated army fled; the SULTAN armies SACKED HAMPI for 6 months — temples demolished, idols broken, statues defaced, libraries burnt — the ONE-TIME ‘greatest city in the world’ (per Domingo Paes) reduced to ruins; never reoccupied as a capital. (6) TIRUMALA (brother of Rama Raya) spirited away Sadashiva Raya + treasury to PENUKONDA (new capital), later shifted to CHANDRAGIRI, then VELLORE. (7) Last Vijayanagara dynasty ARAVIDU continued till 1646. HAMPI ruins: UNESCO World Heritage (1986); Virupaksha, Vitthala, Stone Chariot still stand as testimony.

questions.stem: The ‘AMUKTAMALYADA’, a Telugu literary classic written by Krishnadevaraya, is about:

options.option_text: A story of wars between Pandavas and Kauravas
ANDAL (TAMIL ALVAR SAINT-POETESS) — her devotion to Vishnu; also incorporates a detailed MANUAL OF STATECRAFT (Rajadharma)

questions.explanation: AMUKTAMALYADA (literally ‘she who gives the garland she has worn’) — TELUGU kavya in 6 cantos by KRISHNADEVARAYA himself; one of the FIVE great Telugu kavyas (Pancha Mahakavyas). CONTENT: (1) narrates the legend of GODA DEVI / ANDAL — the 9th-c. Tamil ALVAR saint-poetess of Srivilliputhur, daughter of Periyalvar; she wove a garland daily, wore it herself briefly, and offered it to Lord Vishnu (Ranganatha of Srirangam) — considered sacrilege but accepted by the Lord as a mark of her devotion; she eventually merged into the Ranganatha idol. (2) Includes extensive INTERLUDES ON STATECRAFT (Rajadharma) — Krishnadevaraya’s advice on ministers, diplomacy, famine relief, treatment of subjects, military strategy, forts, water works, foreign trade — a primary source on Vijayanagara polity. Famous line: ‘A crowned king should always rule with an eye to dharma (righteousness)’. Inspired by Krishnadevaraya’s visit to SRIKAKULAM / his patron deity ANDHRA VISHNU appearing in a dream asking him to compose on Goda Devi. OTHER Krishnadevaraya work: JAMBAVATI KALYANAM (Sanskrit, on Krishna-Jambavati wedding).

questions.stem: The ‘Stone Chariot’, an iconic monument of Hampi, is part of the:

options.option_text: VITTHALA TEMPLE complex — built during Deva Raya II / expanded by Krishnadevaraya; dedicated to Vitthala (form of Vishnu); houses 56 musical pillars

questions.explanation: STONE CHARIOT at HAMPI — shrine of GARUDA (Vishnu’s mount) sculpted as a stone CHARIOT; ONE of three famous stone chariots in India (others: KONARK Sun Temple in Odisha, MAHABALIPURAM rathas in TN, and the temple chariot at MELKOTE). LOCATED inside the VITTHALA TEMPLE COMPLEX, Hampi; built in the 16th century under KRISHNADEVARAYA (extending work begun under Deva Raya II). ARCHITECTURAL FEATURES: (1) made of several BLOCKS of granite cleverly joined to look monolithic; (2) wheels were ORIGINALLY rotatable (locked now to prevent damage); (3) two elephants in front — originally horses (whose broken legs can still be seen, elephants added later); (4) depicts Garuda seated inside. Printed on the NEW ₹50 note (2017 Mahatma Gandhi series). Whole VITTHALA temple: famous for MUSICAL PILLARS (SAREGAMA pillars) — 56 pillars that produce different notes when struck. Other Hampi marvels: VIRUPAKSHA temple (oldest, continuously in worship), HAZARA RAMA (royal chapel, walls depict Ramayana), KING’S BALANCE (Tula-Purusha dana place), LOTUS MAHAL (Indo-Islamic), ELEPHANT STABLES, QUEEN’S BATH, MAHANAVAMI DIBBA (Dasara platform). HAMPI declared UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

questions.stem: The ASHTADIGGAJAS (‘eight elephants of literature’) were Telugu poets in the court of:

options.option_text: KRISHNADEVARAYA — TENALI RAMAKRISHNA (the famous jester-poet) was one of them

questions.explanation: ASHTADIGGAJAS (‘eight elephants’ symbolising the eight directions) — EIGHT celebrated TELUGU POETS in KRISHNADEVARAYA’s court (1509-1529), who led the ‘Prabandha era’ — the GOLDEN AGE of Telugu literature. NAMES + works: (1) ALLASANI PEDDANA — ‘ANDHRA KAVITA PITAMAHA’ (father of Telugu poetry); author of MANUCHARITRA / SVAROCHISHA SAMBHAVA. (2) NANDI THIMMANA — PARIJATAPAHARANAMU. (3) MADAYYAGARI MALLANA — RAJASHEKHARA CHARITRA. (4) DHURJATI — KALAHASTI MAHATMYAM, Kalahasti devotional. (5) AYYALARAJU RAMABHADRUDU — RAMABHYUDAYAMU. (6) PINGALI SURANA — RAGHAVAPANDAVIYAMU (simultaneously narrates Ramayana + Mahabharata via clever puns — shlesha poetry). (7) RAMARAJABHUSHANA / BHATTUMURTHI — VASUCHARITRA, NARAKASURA VIJAYAM. (8) TENALI RAMAKRISHNA — author of PANDURANGA MAHATMYA; wit, satirist — innumerable folk tales of his wisdom. Each was a master of a specific style; their works followed the PRABANDHA form (longer literary narrative). They elevated Telugu from an oral/bardic language to a fully classical literary medium. Krishnadevaraya’s court also hosted Sanskrit scholars like VYASATIRTHA (Madhva acharya, Krishnadevaraya's spiritual guide).

questions.stem: Which Portuguese traveller visited the Vijayanagara court of Krishnadevaraya and left a DETAILED account of the capital?

options.option_text: DOMINGO PAES — his ‘Chronica dos Reis de Bisnaga’ describes Hampi as ‘as large as Rome and very beautiful to the sight’; companion FERNAO NUNIZ visited later in Achyutadevaraya’s reign

questions.explanation: DOMINGO PAES (Portuguese horse trader / chronicler) — visited Vijayanagara c. 1520 during KRISHNADEVARAYA’s reign; stayed several months; wrote ‘CHRONICA DOS REIS DE BISNAGA’ (Chronicle of the Kings of Bisnaga [Vijayanagara]). Remarks: (1) described Hampi as ‘AS LARGE AS ROME AND VERY BEAUTIFUL TO THE SIGHT…the best-provided city in the world’; (2) population ~5 lakh; 7 concentric walls; (3) detailed MAHANAVAMI (Dasara) festival with 9-day royal spectacle — elephant processions, wrestling, sacrifices; (4) described BAZAARS selling diamonds, pearls, rubies ‘as if they were breads’; (5) detailed KRISHNADEVARAYA’s physique, daily exercise, military parades. COMPANION FERNAO NUNIZ visited later (1535-37, Achyutadevaraya’s reign), continued the chronicle. OTHER foreign visitors: (1) NICCOLO DE CONTI (Venetian, c. 1420, Deva Raya II) — ‘City has a circumference of 60 miles, 90,000 men fit for arms’. (2) ABDUR RAZZAQ (Persian ambassador from Herat, 1443, Deva Raya II) — ‘The city is such that eye has not seen nor ear heard of any place resembling it upon the whole earth’; described the 7 fortifications, the Mahanavami pavilion. (3) ATHANASIUS NIKITIN (Russian, c. 1470) — Bidar-centric but passed through; noted Hindu-Muslim contrast. (4) LUDOVICO DI VARTHEMA (Italian, early 16th c.). (5) DUARTE BARBOSA (Portuguese, c. 1516).

questions.stem: The capital city of Vijayanagara at HAMPI is situated on the banks of which river?

options.option_text: TUNGABHADRA (formed by confluence of Tunga + Bhadra at Kudli, Karnataka; major tributary of Krishna)

questions.explanation: HAMPI lies on the SOUTHERN bank of the TUNGABHADRA RIVER in the BELLARY district of KARNATAKA (now part of VIJAYANAGARA district, carved out 2021 from Bellary). TUNGABHADRA (‘Pampa’ in ancient texts) — formed by confluence of TUNGA (rises at Gangamoola, Varaha Parvata, Western Ghats) + BHADRA (rises nearby) at KUDLI in Karnataka; flows ~531 km E/NE, joining KRISHNA at Sangameshwaram in Andhra Pradesh. Vijayanagara founders chose the site for its natural defences: (1) Tungabhadra on the north; (2) rocky granite HILLS (Anjana Parvat = Anegundi range) around; (3) strategic; (4) mythological — ancient PAMPA-kshetra where Shiva was worshipped (Virupaksha is Shiva = Pampapati, consort of river-goddess PAMPA). Hampi = corrupted form of Pampa. KISHKINDHA of Ramayana is identified with the Hampi-Anegundi region — monkey kingdom of Sugriva-Hanuman. ANEGUNDI (across the river from Hampi) was the ORIGINAL capital of early Sangamas, before they moved capital to Hampi proper. TUNGABHADRA DAM (Hospet, 1953) built across the river for irrigation + hydropower; joint Karnataka-Andhra project.

questions.stem: The CHIEF SOURCE OF REVENUE in the Vijayanagara empire was:

options.option_text: LAND REVENUE (siddhaya) — 1/6 to 1/3 of produce; supplemented by taxes on trade, tolls, pasture, fish, oil, potter, weaver, and a war-tax (bhandaravadha)

questions.explanation: VIJAYANAGARA ECONOMY — HIGHLY monetised, prosperous, with the land-revenue system called RAYARE-KANDAVARE (or SIDDHAYA). FEATURES: (1) Land revenue the chief income — 1/6 (on wet land, rice) to 1/3 (on irrigated/sugarcane land) of gross produce, paid in cash or kind; (2) AMARAM (military feudal) system: nobles called NAYAKAS / AMARA-NAYAKAS held land in return for maintaining troops — precursor of later Zamindari/Jagirdari system; (3) separate department NAYAKATTANAM administered it; (4) other taxes: SRUTHAYAM (customs), DAIVADAYA (religious), HORSE-TAX, FISHERY, WEAVERS' TAX; (5) EIGHTEEN DIFFERENT TAXES on various trades in major cities; (6) COINS — gold VARAHA / GADYANA (standard coin, ~52 grains), PAGODA (half-varaha), FANAM, PANAMS; copper JITAL; (7) Currency bore Hindu iconography — Garuda, Vishnu, Hanuman, boar (Varaha, royal emblem of Sangamas & Tuluvas). COMMERCE: FLOURISHING FOREIGN TRADE via ports GOA, BHATKAL, HONAVAR, MANGALORE, CAMBAY, PULICAT; (a) Exported textiles, rice, iron, diamonds, sandalwood, spices; (b) imported horses (from ARABIA/PERSIA via Portuguese trade — essential for cavalry), elephants, silks, pearls, gems, precious metals. Indigenous industries: weaving, metalwork, jewellery, dyeing.

questions.stem: The FOUR successive dynasties that ruled Vijayanagara (in chronological order) were:
questions.explanation: FOUR VIJAYANAGARA DYNASTIES: (1) SANGAMA (1336-1485, ~150 years) — founders; Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Deva Raya I (digged Tungabhadra-anicut), Deva Raya II (Prauda Deva, ‘Immadi Deva Raya’, Niccolo de Conti, Abdur Razzaq visited), Mallikarjuna, Virupaksha II. Named after Sangama (father of Harihara and Bukka). (2) SALUVA (1485-1505) — founded by SALUVA NARASIMHA, a noble who usurped throne in the ‘First usurpation’ (1485) amid Sangama weakness. Lasted only 20 years; Immadi Narasimha succeeded as a minor. (3) TULUVA (1491-1570) — founded by TULUVA NARASA NAYAKA, regent who usurped power in the ‘Second usurpation’ (1503-05) from the Saluvas. His sons Vira Narasimha, KRISHNADEVARAYA (1509-29, golden age), Achyutadevaraya (1529-42), Venkata I, and Sadashiva Raya (nominal till 1570; real power with Rama Raya of Aravidu family). (4) ARAVIDU (1542-1646) — founded by TIRUMALA (Rama Raya's brother) after Battle of Talikota (1565); fled with Sadashiva + treasury; ruled from PENUKONDA (Anantapur district) → CHANDRAGIRI (Chittoor) → VELLORE; Venkata II (height of Aravidu rule), Sriranga III (last). Empire finally extinguished by 1646 (Sultanates of Bijapur and Golconda dismembered it). VIJAYANAGARA = 310 years of continuous Hindu imperial rule in south India.
